_comment: Staged bring-up: channel 4 is the only bidirectional channel here, isolating whether its AM32 instance actually supports bidir DShot before it's ever combined with the others. Short (1 minute) - this is a smoke test, not a soak. min_record_rate_hz=500: see single_channel_baseline.json's comment - confirmed with clean single-channel runs at 566-588/s, real margin without being toothless. UNRESOLVED as of 2026-08-30: two identical runs of this scenario with the idle motor at pin8 on sm_id=4 (same PIO1 block as the sm6/rx7 bidir pair) both got a reproducible ~322/s record rate (well under min_record_rate_hz) and failed - not a one-off glitch. Moved pin8 to sm_id=1 (PIO0, off the bidir pair's block) as an UNTESTED hypothesis - idle-motor-sharing-the-bidir-block was previously assumed harmless under literal irq(4) (a non-bidir motor never touches the IRQ), but that assumption has not been re-examined for the current rel()-based mechanism, and three PIO programs (dshot, dshot_bidir_tx, dshot_bidir_rx) sharing one block's instruction memory is also an unexplored variable. This edit has NOT been run - do that first, next session, before trusting this file again.
